Read-only survey. Do NOT modify any file or run any git command that changes state.

Target: the unmerged worktree `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals` (commit message starts "wip(domain): every version draws every arrow's push…"). Compare it against `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst` (main, commit 48eb562).

I need a precise, quantitative picture of TWO things in that worktree:

(1) **The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths.** Find the code that makes each of the 2000 parameter "versions" draw a per-arrow strength (rather than only per-claim priors). Report: which files and functions changed, exact added/deleted line counts (`git diff --stat` against the merge-base is fine — read-only), how the spread is derived from provenance (what the mapping from provenance category to a strength range is, and where that mapping is written down), what tests exist for it, and whether it changes the Hormuz demo numbers. The brief I was given says "on the strike branch two claims fall to `unchanged`" — find the evidence for that claim in the worktree (a test, a golden fixture, a STATUS note, a commit message) and quote it.

(2) **The path product moved into `domain/`.** Find the code implementing INV-8 ("every path shows its multiplied-out likelihood beside the story"). Report file:line, how many lines, what it computes exactly (which numbers are multiplied, read on which days), which route/API field carries it, what the Verify door reports today, and which tests cover it. Also check whether it is currently behind a flag / on hold.

Also report: total `git diff --stat` of the worktree against main (files, insertions, deletions); which branch/commit it sits on; whether its tests pass is NOT needed (do not run the suite — you may run at most one single test file if it is small and fast, but prefer reading).

Return: a factual report with absolute file paths, line counts, and quoted code where the exact text matters. No recommendations.

Kent Gang <oddlyimproper@gmail.com>
Mon Sep 21 16:01:36 2026 +0300

wip(domain): every version draws every arrow's push as wide as its receipt says

Record 0014's provenance-derived spread, in the engine and its tests. The chapter
sweep it must travel with is NOT in this commit — that is the next step.

Each of the 2 000 versions now draws every arrow's push from a bell curve centred
on the push the map states, as wide as where the arrow came from says
(`PROVENANCE_SPREAD`), on the log-odds scale the push is already written in. The
draw stream is per arrow, keyed by the seed and the arrow's own identifier
exactly as the per-claim streams are, so adding an arrow cannot move another
arrow's draws. There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`.

A drawn push never changes the shape of the map: which arrows oppose a
supposition, and the day one undermines it, are still read off the stated
strength, because a retraction is one record on one world.

`test_band_is_not_sampling_noise` now freezes priors AND pushes, through a
private `_propagate_with_no_spread` rather than a knob on `propagate` — a world
built with a different spread table could not be rebuilt by `versions_of`.
`test_range_matches_analytic_first_order_on_fixture` gained the strength terms
and its tolerance tightened from .02 to .01; the two methods agree to .005 or
better on every claim of the fixture.

Two numbers on the worked example moved, both honestly: B on the strike branch
and N1 now read `unchanged`, because two large opposing pushes nearly cancel on B
and because the only arrow into N1 is the map's one `asserted` arrow. The rail
loses N1. Full numbers in the report.

            "it says which of the two it is."

def verdict(
    graph: Graph,
    destination: PropositionId,
    *,
    beliefs: Mapping[PropositionId, Belief] | None = None,
) -> Verdict:
    """Grade the route from the claim the map started at to the destination.

    The route shown is the **best-backed** one: over every route, the one whose
    weakest arrow is strongest, by the map's own rule.

    An honest caveat belongs beside the multiplied-out number wherever it is
    shown: it multiplies likelihoods each read on a different day, so it is not a
    joint probability.

    Args:
        graph: The finished map.
        destination: The claim the person asked whether the story reaches.
        beliefs: The worked-through likelihood of every claim, when the numbers
            have been run. Without them the route is still graded structurally and
            the multiplied-out number is absent rather than invented.

    Returns:
        A route and its number, or an honest statement that there is none.
    """
    routes = best_backed_routes(graph, frozenset({graph.hypothesis_id}))
    claims = {claim.id: claim for claim in graph.propositions}
    wanted = claims[destination].claim

    reached = routes.get(destination)
    if reached is not None and len(reached.path) > 1:
        return Verdict(
            kind="reached",
            path=reached.path,
            product=_multiplied_out(reached.path, beliefs),
            why=(
                f"The story reaches {wanted} in {len(reached.path) - 1} steps, "
                "along the best-backed route on this map."
            ),
        )

    touching, hops = _nearest_to(graph, destination, routes)
    if touching is not None:
        return Verdict(
            kind="no_path",
            nearest=touching,
            why=(
                f"Nothing on this map reaches {wanted}. The closest claim the "
                f"story does reach is {claims[touching].claim}, {hops} arrows away "
                "from it."
            ),
        )
    best_backed = _best_backed_end(graph, routes)
    if best_backed is None:
        return Verdict(
            kind="no_path",
            why=f"Nothing on this map reaches {wanted}. The story never left where it started.",
        )
    return Verdict(
        kind="no_path",
        nearest=best_backed,
        why=(
            f"Nothing on this map reaches {wanted}, and no arrow on it touches "
            f"that claim at all. The best-backed thing the story does reach is "
            f"{claims[best_backed].claim}."
        ),
    )


def _multiplied_out(
    route: Sequence[PropositionId], beliefs: Mapping[PropositionId, Belief] | None
) -> float | None:
    """Multiply the likelihoods along a route together.

    The claim the map started from is left out: it is what the person is supposing
    happens, so it is not one of the steps that has to go right.

    The map's own arithmetic has no such number today — nothing in `domain/`
    multiplies a route out — so it is worked out here, over numbers the map
    produced. It moves the day it does.

    Args:
        route: The route, claim by claim, starting at the claim the map started
            from.
        beliefs: The worked-through likelihood of every claim, or nothing at all.

    Returns:
        The product, or nothing at all when the numbers have not been run.
    """
    if beliefs is None:
        return None
    product = 1.0
    for claim_id in route[1:]:
        found = beliefs.get(claim_id)
        if found is None:
            return None
        product *= found.p
    return product


def _nearest_to(
    graph: Graph, destination: PropositionId, routes: Mapping[PropositionId, Route]
) -> tuple[PropositionId | None, int]:
    """Find the claim the story reached that is fewest arrows from the destination.

    Arrows are walked in either direction here, because the question is how close
    the map came and not which way the causing ran. That is a different question
    from choosing a route, which is why it is not the map's route rule.

    When nothing on the map touches the destination, there is no such distance,
    and we do not guess at one: nothing comes back, and the caller says so in
    plain words instead.

    Args:
        graph: The finished map.
        destination: The claim the person asked about.
        routes: Every claim the story reaches, by the map's own route rule.

    Returns:
        That claim and how many arrows away it is, or nothing at all and zero.

    reached = set(routes) - {destination}
    hops = {destination: 0}
    waiting = [destination]
    while waiting:
        here = waiting.pop(0)

# --- The range is how sure we are of the numbers, not how the dice fell ------


def test_band_is_not_sampling_noise() -> None:
    """Take every number on the map down to a point and the band collapses.

    This is the single most likely way to get the engine wrong. An implementation
    that reported how much its own sampling wobbled would pass every other test in
    this file and fail here, loudly: with nothing uncertain left anywhere on the
    map there is nothing for a band to be about, so there must be no band.

    **Two things have to be frozen now, not one.** A version of the map draws a
    likelihood for every claim's prior *and* a push for every arrow, so freezing
    the priors alone leaves the arrows still varying and leaves a band that is
    perfectly real. Both go: `_frozen` rewrites the priors as points and
    `_propagate_with_no_spread` holds every push at exactly what the map states.

+    """The word on the row is the rule applied to the two numbers beside it.

+    own cannot tell "it barely moved" from "nobody agrees which way it went".

+    for claim_id, one in answer.claims.items():

+            assert one.unchanged_because is None, claim_id
+            continue

+            assert one.unchanged_because == "under_the_floor", claim_id
+        elif one.agreement is not None and one.agreement < 0.90:
+            assert one.unchanged_because == "versions_disagree", claim_id
+        else:
+            assert one.unchanged_because is None, claim_id
+
+

+    """Every other word means the test did not fail, so there is no half to name.
+
+    On the worked example's strike branch: claims that moved, the claim the
+    branch added, and a claim forced false all carry nothing at all, and the
+    claims that held still all carry a word.
+    """
+    base = _hormuz_world(None)
+    strike = _hormuz_world(HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE)
+    answer = diff(base, strike, edit_in_words=HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE.label)
+    assert not isinstance(answer, list), answer
+
+    held_still = [one for one in answer.claims.values() if one.state == "unchanged"]
+    moved = [one for one in answer.claims.values() if one.state != "unchanged"]
+    assert held_still and moved, "the worked example was expected to show both"
+    assert all(one.unchanged_because is not None for one in held_still), held_still
+    assert all(one.unchanged_because is None for one in moved), moved
+
+    cut = _hormuz_world(_branch(Do(target="C", value=False, at=FIXTURE_DATE)), **SMALL)
+    forced = diff(_hormuz_world(None, **SMALL), cut, edit_in_words="The premium never falls")

+

+    to act on, because a move nobody would notice needs no second sentence about
+    its direction. The claim is the one an observation moves through the version
+    weights alone — its move is tiny and its same-direction share is zero — and
+    the test finds it by those two facts rather than by name.
+    """

+    observed = _hormuz_world(_branch(Observe(target="B", value=True)))
+    answer = diff(base, observed, edit_in_words="Brent settled below $68")
+    assert not isinstance(answer, list), answer
+
+    failing_both = [
+        one
+        for one in answer.claims.values()
+        if one.state == "unchanged"

+        and one.agreement is not None
+        and one.agreement < 0.90
+    ]

+    """The reweighting field is the fuller answer, and neither field replaces the other.
+

+    nothing, so the half it failed is the same-direction half — and the reason it
+    failed is the one `moved_only_by_reweighting` states. Both are true, both are
+    carried, and the Inspector shows the fuller one.
+    """
+    base = _hormuz_world(None)
+    observed = _hormuz_world(_branch(Observe(target="C", value=True)))
+    answer = diff(base, observed, edit_in_words="the premium printed below 0.4%")
+    assert not isinstance(answer, list), answer
+
+    reweighted = [one for one in answer.claims.values() if one.moved_only_by_reweighting]
+    assert reweighted, "the worked example was expected to show one"
+    for one in reweighted:
+        assert one.state == "unchanged"
+        assert one.unchanged_because == "versions_disagree"

diff --git a/backend/tests/unit/domain/test_diff.py b/backend/tests/unit/domain/test_diff.py
index 1695c54..bcc9cde 100644
--- a/backend/tests/unit/domain/test_diff.py
+++ b/backend/tests/unit/domain/test_diff.py
@@ -982,6 +982,114 @@ def test_no_direction_at_all_when_no_version_counted_in_both_numbers() -> None:
         assert not one.moved_only_by_reweighting, claim_id
     assert answer.rows == (), "no ending can be listed as moved when no direction can be read"
     assert SECOND_SENTENCE.match(answer.summary), answer.summary
+    for claim_id, one in answer.claims.items():
+        # No direction was readable, so the second half of the test never ran and
+        # there is no honest way to say it failed. Where the move is under the
+        # floor the first half did run, and that answer stands on its own.
+        assert one.unchanged_because in {None, "under_the_floor"}, claim_id
+        if one.unchanged_because is None:
+            assert one.delta is None or abs(one.delta) >= 0.005, claim_id
+
+
+# --- Which half of the test an unchanged claim failed ----------------------
+
+
+@given(st.data())
+@many
+def test_an_unchanged_claim_says_which_half_it_failed(data: st.DataObject) -> None:
+    """The word on the row is the rule applied to the two numbers beside it.
+
+    Both constants live in the engine and reach no reader, so *unchanged* on its
+    own cannot tell "it barely moved" from "nobody agrees which way it went".
+    The word says which. Nothing here is typed in: the expected answer is worked
+    out from the row's own `delta` and `agreement`, so the row has to be
+    self-consistent for every map a generator can produce.
+    """
+    graph = data.draw(graphs())
+    answer = _compared(graph, data.draw(branches(graph)), data.draw(branches(graph)))
+
+    for claim_id, one in answer.claims.items():
+        if one.state != "unchanged" or one.delta is None:
+            assert one.unchanged_because is None, claim_id
+            continue
+        if abs(one.delta) < 0.005:
+            assert one.unchanged_because == "under_the_floor", claim_id
+        elif one.agreement is not None and one.agreement < 0.90:
+            assert one.unchanged_because == "versions_disagree", claim_id
+        else:
+            assert one.unchanged_because is None, claim_id
+
+
+def test_only_an_unchanged_claim_says_which_half_it_failed() -> None:
+    """Every other word means the test did not fail, so there is no half to name.
+
+    On the worked example's strike branch: claims that moved, the claim the
+    branch added, and a claim forced false all carry nothing at all, and the
+    claims that held still all carry a word.
+    """
+    base = _hormuz_world(None)
+    strike = _hormuz_world(HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE)
+    answer = diff(base, strike, edit_in_words=HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE.label)
+    assert not isinstance(answer, list), answer
+
+    held_still = [one for one in answer.claims.values() if one.state == "unchanged"]
+    moved = [one for one in answer.claims.values() if one.state != "unchanged"]
+    assert held_still and moved, "the worked example was expected to show both"
+    assert all(one.unchanged_because is not None for one in held_still), held_still
+    assert all(one.unchanged_because is None for one in moved), moved
+
+    cut = _hormuz_world(_branch(Do(target="C", value=False, at=FIXTURE_DATE)), **SMALL)
+    forced = diff(_hormuz_world(None, **SMALL), cut, edit_in_words="The premium never falls")
+    assert not isinstance(forced, list), forced
+    assert forced.claims["C"].state == "killed"
+    assert forced.claims["C"].unchanged_because is None
+
+
+def test_the_floor_is_read_first_when_a_claim_fails_both_halves() -> None:
+    """A claim that barely moved and disagreed about it says it barely moved.
+
+    Two true answers, and something has to choose; the floor is the cheaper fact
+    to act on, because a move nobody would notice needs no second sentence about
+    its direction. The claim is the one an observation moves through the version
+    weights alone — its move is tiny and its same-direction share is zero — and
+    the test finds it by those two facts rather than by name.
+    """
=== ADR 0014 spread mentions ===
19:Stack 03a is about to write the engine, and two rules it cannot be written without are unsettled. The first: the showcase branch supposes the strait is open on 1 October, then inserts a strike on the 2nd that pushes against it. What happens to the supposed claim, and on which day does it stop being taken as given? The second: every claim shows a range — `.35 (.20–.49)` — and nothing says what that range *is*. Record 0005 called it "a standard interval for such a share" and admitted in the same breath that it mixes simulation noise with the elicited spread, which means the width shrinks by running the machine longer. A number that moves when you buy more computer time is not telling you anything about the world. So: **when does a supposition end, and what does the range under a computed likelihood mean?**
46:* **R3.** Twenty batches of five hundred worlds, the band read off the spread between batches — record 0005's "standard interval for such a share", made concrete.
89:1. Draw **two thousand versions of the map** by Latin hypercube sampling — a way of spreading draws evenly instead of letting them clump; three lines of `numpy`, no new dependency. Each version draws every claim's likelihood from that claim's own stated range. A version is **one coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind**, never "every low end at once".
93:**The noise correction, in words.** The spread we measure across versions is the real spread we want *plus* the wobble of having run only eight worlds each. Those two add, so subtract the second and shrink the band by what is left — the law of total variance. In symbols:
103:* `v_k` — the spread (variance) of those `m` computed probabilities within version `k`; `v_k / m` is how much version `k`'s answer wobbles for sampling reasons alone.
104:* `V` — the spread (variance) of `q_1 … q_2000` across versions. This is the quantity that is too wide.
105:* `f` — the shrink factor, 0 to 1. Clamped at 0, so a claim whose apparent spread was all noise reports a zero-width band rather than an imaginary number.
111:**Link strengths are fixed numbers in stack 03a**, and the propagation chapter says so in those words. Only the claims' likelihoods vary between versions. Spreading the strengths too is decision G.
140:**Rank = size of the move × the weakest provenance weight on the shortest path from the edit to that terminal.** Two factors, and only two. **Range width and agreement are shown as their own columns and never multiplied in** — multiplying width in would sink exactly the claims FR-21 floats, which is the opposite of the advice the user wants.
154:* **A spread on link strengths derived from provenance** — a cited arrow narrow, a bare story wide, at no extra elicitation cost. **Stack 04**, when the backing is real; in 03a every fixture arrow is hand-written `argued` or `asserted`, so the spread would be uniform and teach nobody anything. **There are no `strength_lo` / `strength_hi` fields, ever** — record 0005's "one number and one sentence per link" stands.
241:* **Input to a stack 04 decision, not a decision here — stated ranges from language models are reliably too narrow.** FermiEval (2025): a nominal 90 per cent range covered the truth 28 per cent of the time; QuantSightBench (2026) reproduced it; Paleka et al. (ICLR 2025) found stated ranges incoherent under rewording; Farquhar et al. (*Nature*, 2024) found measured disagreement across runs beats self-report; Halawi (2024) and the AIA Forecaster (2025) both ensemble. The likely shape: a trimmed mean for the point, and the wider of the stated range and the measured spread for the range, the measured number being *agreement*.

content.content:
179:It is tested rather than asserted: `test_a_days_answer_does_not_depend_on_which_other_days_were_worked_out` works one map out twice — on the grid the engine chooses, and on every day of the window through `_versions_on_every_day`, a private seam in `propagation.py` that exists for this and is reachable from nothing that ships — and requires every number behind every claim to agree **bit for bit** on every day the two share, for every version. Both runs are taken before either is read. The map carries one of every shape a push can have (a spike with a half-life, a step, a ramp, a sustaining arrow, lags on all of them) over a nine-hundred-day window, and the test runs it under a supposition, under an observation, under both together, and under **a supposition something later undermines** — the likeliest place for a day to depend on the day before it. `test_the_grid_is_safe_on_maps_nobody_wrote_by_hand` asks the same question of generated maps and generated branches, because whether a thinned grid happens to miss a firing day depends on how a map's dates fall, and one hand-written map is one arrangement of dates.
261:> N1's move is the largest on the map and the change list still leaves it off, because the only arrow into it is the map's one `asserted` arrow and a push nobody could back is drawn so wide that the versions do not agree which way it went. [`diff.md`](diff.md) B4 works that through; it is the clearest thing the spread does on this fixture.
281:**What a supposed claim's `Belief` holds.** While a supposition holds the claim is true in every draw, so its `Belief` is `p = lo = hi = 1.0` — or `0.0` where it was supposed false. That exists for exactly one reader: the path product (INV-8, the rule that a chain's multiplied-out likelihood is reported honestly), which needs a factor to multiply. **No other surface may read it.** Every other reader checks `states` first and prints the word *Supposed*, because a tile showing `1.00` claims a certainty about the world that the user never asserted — they asserted a supposition.
327:| `documented` · `historical` · `market_implied` — somebody fetched something | `0.15` |
328:| `argued` · `user` — a stated mechanism, or a person's own judgement | `0.40` |
329:| `simulated` — a probe's output | `0.50` |
330:| `asserted` — a sentence with no mechanism in it | `0.60` |
334:* **It is measured in log-odds**, the scale a push is already written in. A width of `0.40` is four tenths of a log-odds unit, not four tenths of the push, so a weak arrow and a strong one with the same receipt are drawn equally wide.
335:* **A weakly-backed push can come out the other way round in some versions**, and that is the honest reading: *we cannot vouch for which way this one goes* is most of what `asserted` means. [`diff.md`](diff.md) B4 shows the consequence on this very fixture.
341:**A generated map's arrows are only ever `documented` or `argued`** — the accept step writes `documented` when the search returned an address the arrow cites and `argued` otherwise, and the map's own rules refuse an arrow with no mechanism at all. The other four words are written by somebody else: a stored example, a person, a price adapter, a probe.
508:**9. Do not add `strength_lo` and `strength_hi` to make arrows uncertain.** *Because* every arrow in today's fixture is hand-written `argued` or `asserted`, so spreading them now would widen everything by the same amount and teach nobody anything — and a second elicited pair per arrow is exactly the budget record 0005 refused. **Do** keep strengths fixed in 03a and derive the spread from `provenance` in stack 04, where "how well-backed" becomes "how wide" at no extra elicitation cost.

4:+++ b/spec/multiverse/propagation.md
10:+**Three things that are deliberately absent.** There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, now or ever *(and that is still true now that arrows vary — see B5's rule, which derives how wide a push is drawn from where the arrow came from, every time it is needed)*. There is no `scipy`: the Latin hypercube — a way of spreading draws evenly instead of letting them clump — is three lines of `numpy`, and the percentiles are one. And there is no module-level random generator — see B7.
11:+
12:+*(Amended 2026-09-21. This paragraph said link strengths were fixed numbers and that widening an arrow would ship in stack 04. It shipped: every version now draws every arrow's push as well as every claim's prior. The rule is in B5 and the three streams are in B7. Nothing was added to store it — the first half of the sentence, no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, is exactly what "derived, never stored" means.)*
13:+
14:+**What the spread costs.** Nothing the table above could show. A version drawing a push per arrow is one number per arrow per version — on this map seven arrows × 2 000 versions, about a tenth of a megabyte — against the claims × days × 16 000 worlds those rows are made of. They were measured before arrows varied and are not re-measured for it.
23:+> **On the Hormuz map.** B's prior is `.28`, whose log-odds is `−0.94`. On the strike branch, day 1: `S → B` is an impulse with `lag=0.0`, so it is already at full size — `−2.4`. `H → B` has not arrived (two-day lag); `C → B` has not arrived (seven-day lag); `R → B` has not arrived (five days from R's day zero). Total `−0.94 − 2.4 = −3.34`, about **`.03`** by hand. Day 2: `H → B` arrives at full size, `+1.6`, and `S → B` has faded by one day of its ten-day half-life to `−2.24`. Total `−1.58`, about **`.17`** by hand. **The engine reports `.039` and `.19`**, seed `20261001` — a hair above the hand sums, for the same reason as in B4: each is an average across two thousand versions, and that average sits above the middle whenever the likelihood is below `.5`. B *rises* between day 1 and day 2 either way, and that rise is golden assertion 4.
32:+> **On the Hormuz map.** `H → B` is a trigger that fired on day 0, so on day 2 it delivers `+1.6` to B even though H's supposition was withdrawn on day 1 — that domino is down. `H → C` is a sustain, so from day 1 its `+1.1` is present only in the draws where H still came out true, which after day 4 is about nine in a hundred. Same cause, two honest behaviours, one branch.
35:+> The clearest reading of the difference is **N1**, *Omani-mediated talks resume publicly*. `H → N1` is a trigger, and H was supposed true on day 0, so it fired in **every** world. The strike then withdraws H — and N1 still comes out **higher** on the strike branch than in the base world, `.38` against `.28`, because that domino cannot be stood back up. Meanwhile C, held by a sustain arrow from the same claim, collapses from `.40` to `.074`. One cause, one branch, two claims moving in opposite directions, and the only difference between them is a single field on the arrow.
36:+>
37:+> N1's move is the largest on the map and the change list still leaves it off, because the only arrow into it is the map's one `asserted` arrow and a push nobody could back is drawn so wide that the versions do not agree which way it went. [`diff.md`](diff.md) B4 works that through; it is the clearest thing the spread does on this fixture.
46:+> | Oct 5 onward | **about `.086`**, the series marked *pushed* | `S → H`'s step reaches full size — `−1.9` on a log-odds baseline of `−0.62` — and pushes `H` down |
51:+> The engine's own figures, seed `20261001`: `.356` on the withdrawn days and `.086` from Oct 5. Do the two sums by hand and you get `.35` and `sigmoid(−2.52) = .074` — both right as hand arithmetic. The reported numbers sit a hair above because each is a mean across two thousand versions, and that mean sits above the middle whenever the likelihood is below `.5`; B5 explains it. The gap is wider now that the versions draw the pushes as well as the priors, for the same reason and no other. Where this chapter quotes a number the engine reported, it is the engine's.
60:+* **How sure we are of the numbers we put in.** Every prior on the map was elicited, and **every arrow's push was written down by somebody with more or less to go on**. A different but equally defensible set of those numbers would give a different `p`. **That** is the range.
68:+#### How wide an arrow's push is drawn — the rule, stated once
69:+
70:+*(Added 2026-09-21. Kent settled it in decision record 0014 and deferred it to stack 04, because every arrow on this fixture is hand-written and generation is what finally makes arrows differ. Every other chapter cites this paragraph rather than re-deciding it.)*
71:+
72:+**How well-backed an arrow is becomes how wide it is, and nobody is asked a second question.** An arrow carries a `provenance` — a receipt our own pipeline writes from what actually happened, never something a model claims for itself — and that receipt is the one thing on an arrow that already says how much there was to go on. So each version of the map draws every arrow's push from a bell curve centred on the push the map states, this wide:
73:+
74:+| Where the arrow came from | How wide the push is drawn |
75:+|---|---|
76:+| `documented` · `historical` · `market_implied` — somebody fetched something | `0.15` |
77:+| `argued` · `user` — a stated mechanism, or a person's own judgement | `0.40` |
78:+| `simulated` — a probe's output | `0.50` |
79:+| `asserted` — a sentence with no mechanism in it | `0.60` |
80:+
81:+Four things the rule means, each of which somebody will otherwise get wrong:
82:+
83:+* **It is measured in log-odds**, the scale a push is already written in. A width of `0.40` is four tenths of a log-odds unit, not four tenths of the push, so a weak arrow and a strong one with the same receipt are drawn equally wide.
84:+* **A weakly-backed push can come out the other way round in some versions**, and that is the honest reading: *we cannot vouch for which way this one goes* is most of what `asserted` means. [`diff.md`](diff.md) B4 shows the consequence on this very fixture.
85:+* **There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, now or ever** (Kent, record 0014). The width is derived from the receipt every time it is needed. A stored width would be a second number about one arrow, and the two would drift.
86:+* **A drawn push never changes the *shape* of the map.** Which arrows oppose a supposition, and the day one of them undermines it, are read off the strength the map *states* — the same answer in every version, because a retraction is one record on one world and cannot be true in version 7 and false in version 8. A drawn push decides only how hard that arrow shoves inside its own version.
87:+
88:+Not to be confused with the *other* table that reads the same receipt: [`diff.md`](diff.md)'s provenance **weight**, which turns it into how well-backed a *route* is for the change list's ranking. Two questions, two tables. Merging them would make a well-backed arrow's rank depend on how sure we are of its number.
89:+
90:+**A generated map's arrows are only ever `documented` or `argued`** — the accept step writes `documented` when the search returned an address the arrow cites and `argued` otherwise, and the map's own rules refuse an arrow with no mechanism at all. The other four words are written by somebody else: a stored example, a person, a price adapter, a probe.
91:+
95:+1. Draw **2 000 versions** of the map: a likelihood for every claim's prior, from the fitted shape above, **and a push for every arrow**, from the rule above. A Latin hypercube either way — a way of spreading draws evenly instead of letting them clump. `numpy` only, three lines. A version is **one coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind**, never "every low end at once".
104:+**Four designs, measured on 2026-09-17** — on Hormuz claim B read at **day 45**, against the exact answer by enumeration, `.35 (.20–.49)`. This is a dated comparison of four *designs*, so it is kept as it was measured; B's resolve-by day has since moved to day 14, and the shipped engine reports `.35 (.20–.50)` for B at day 45 *(re-measured 2026-09-21, now that the versions draw the pushes too; it read `.35 (.20–.49)` before)*.
113:+The delta method is kept — not as the engine, but as a **cross-check in a test**, and it now carries a term per arrow as well as a term per prior. On the shipped engine, B in the base world on its own resolve-by day: the sampler reports `.2424–.5564` and the analytic answer is `.2394–.5562`. Two independent methods, agreeing to two significant figures.
118:+**The shares do not add up to the whole band, and should not be read as though they did** *(added 2026-09-21)*. They answer *whose **prior*** explains this width, and a version now draws the arrows' pushes as well; what the pushes explain is in neither table. On B in the base world the seven shares total **72%**, and the missing quarter is the arrows.
119:+
120:+On the shipped fixture, B in the base world read on its own resolve-by day: **58% of B's band is B's own prior**, then H at 5.0% and C at 3.8%. Pin B's prior down — freeze it at a point — and the band goes from `.24–.56` to `.32–.48`: **from 31 points wide to 16**. That is the ranking FR-21 asks for, in one number per claim. (FR-21 and record 0014 say "its own base rate"; the thing that varies between versions is the claim's `prior`, which is the word used here.)
126:+* **A `do` does not reliably narrow what is downstream.** It collapses the target's own band, but B's width goes *up* under `do(H)` — `.314` to `.380`, measured — because the logistic curve is steeper where the answer lands. The honest thing to show is the **share**, not the width: H's contribution to B's band falls from **5.0% to 0.6%**, which is the sentence a reader can act on.
127:+* **A terminal's band is dominated by its own prior.** An upstream range reaches it multiplied by `p(1−p)`, which is at most a quarter. Do not build the demo around "widen H and watch B widen": double H's stated range on the log-odds scale — both halves — and B's band widens by **8%**, from `.314` to `.340`.
136:+### B7 — Three seed streams, and replay
141:+There are **three streams** *(the third added 2026-09-21, with the spread on the arrows)*, and keeping them apart is load-bearing:
146:+| `params` | The outer loop — which likelihood each of the 2 000 versions gives each claim's prior | **Must not depend on the branch.** A base world and a branch world built from the same seed use the *same* 2 000 versions |
147:+| `strengths` | The outer loop — which push each of those versions gives each arrow | The same rule, for the same reason |
151:+**Every stream is derived per thing**, from the seed and a hash of that claim's or that arrow's **own** identifier. So adding a claim cannot shift any other claim's draws and **adding an arrow cannot shift any other arrow's** — a thing's numbers depend on its own name and the seed, and on nothing about how many neighbours it has or what order they were written in. That is what makes `test_versions_do_not_depend_on_the_branch` and `test_adding_an_arrow_does_not_move_another_arrows_draws` hold *exactly* rather than approximately, and it is also what makes the dice cancel out of a paired comparison: version *k* of the base world and version *k* of the branch world drew the same numbers for every claim and every arrow they share.
156:+> **On the Hormuz map.** Supposing the strait opens moves B, on its own resolve-by day, from `.40 (.24–.56)` to `.58 (.38–.76)`. The two bands **overlap from `.38` to `.56`** — more than half the narrower of the two — and a reader comparing bands would call that inconclusive. Compare the same versions against each other instead and **99.9% of them move the same way**, by `+.19` (`+.084` to `+.29` eight times in ten); [`diff.md`](diff.md) owns that number and the rule that reads it. Band overlap would report "no change" about the single clearest change on the map.
168:+| **H** the strait reopens | `.36 (.22–.50)` | `.086 (.034–.15)` | the supposition is withdrawn and then pushed down |
169:+| **C** the premium falls below 0.4% | `.40 (.25–.56)` | `.074 (.029–.13)` | `S → C` holds the premium up |
170:+| **B** Brent below $68 | `.40 (.24–.56)` | `.31 (.16–.48)` | the strike puts the risk premium back in the price |
171:+| **R** OPEC+ restraint | `.19 (.080–.32)` | `.19 (.080–.32)` | **byte-identical** — reached only by a feedback arrow |
175:+| **M2** XLE against SPY | `.43 (.28–.59)` | `.36 (.23–.51)` | tradeable |
176:+| **N1** talks resume | `.28 (.15–.44)` | `.38 (.17–.61)` | **up**, and the widest band on the map — see B3 |

# Survey report — `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals`

## 0. Position and totals

- **Branch:** `feat/04b-evals`, HEAD = `a59409c` *"wip(domain): every version draws every arrow's push as wide as its receipt says"*.
- **Merge-base with `main` = `48eb562`** — i.e. main's tip. Nothing to rebase.
- Two commits ahead: `21c0e05` (evals harness) then `a59409c` (the spread).
- **The worktree is dirty and was being actively edited while I surveyed it** (mtimes 16:34–16:36; `README.md` currently contains unresolved placeholders `<<COUNT: server>>`, `<<COUNT: browser>>`, `<<COUNT: end-to-end>>`). Numbers below are a snapshot.

| Scope | Files | Insertions | Deletions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Committed only (`main...HEAD`) | 20 | 2 699 | 81 |
| Uncommitted (`HEAD` → worktree) | 9 | 348 | 80 |
| **Total worktree vs `48eb562`** | **27** | **3 047** | **161** |

`a59409c` alone is 3 files, **+461 / −42**: `backend/src/katalyst/domain/propagation.py` +262/−22, `backend/tests/unit/domain/test_propagation.py` +180/−9, `backend/tests/unit/domain/test_diff.py` +19/−11.

---

## 1. The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths

### Files and functions

**`/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/src/katalyst/domain/propagation.py` (+262 / −22, committed in `a59409c`)**

| line | symbol | what |
|---|---|---|
| 118 | `STRENGTHS_STREAM = 3` | new third RNG stream, alongside `PARAMS_STREAM = 1` (priors) and `WORLDS_STREAM = 2` |
| 126 | `PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[Provenance, float]` | **the mapping** (below) |
| 172 | `NO_SPREAD` | `dict.fromkeys(PROVENANCE_SPREAD, 0.0)` — test-only |
| 453 | `propagate(...)` | now a thin wrapper that calls `_propagated(..., spreads=PROVENANCE_SPREAD)` |
| 516 | `_propagated(...)` | new private body, takes `spreads` |
| 560 | `_propagate_with_no_spread(...)` | new; test-only seam |
| 1346 | `_Sample.strengths: Mapping[LinkId, Numbers]` | new field on the sample record |
| 1353 | `_stream_key(identifier: str)` | **renamed** from `_claim_key(identifier: PropositionId)`, now keyed by claim *or* arrow id |
| 1507 | `_version_strengths(arrow, seed, versions, spreads)` | new, ~30 lines — the draw itself |
| 1625 | `_one_pass(..., strengths, ...)` | new parameter; the push term changed |

`versions_of` (line 622 region) and `_versions_on_every_day` were both updated to pass `spreads=PROVENANCE_SPREAD` so a world can still be rebuilt from `(graph, branch, seed)`.

### How the spread is derived, and where the mapping is written down

Two places, and they agree.

**(a) Code — `propagation.py:126`:**

```python
PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[Provenance, float] = MappingProxyType(
    {
        "documented": 0.15,
        "historical": 0.15,
        "market_implied": 0.15,
        "argued": 0.40,
        "user": 0.40,
        "simulated": 0.50,
        "asserted": 0.60,
    }
)
```

All seven members of `Provenance` (`/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/src/katalyst/domain/link.py:39`) are covered. There is **no** `get_args`-based exhaustiveness test.

**(b) Spec — `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/spec/multiverse/propagation.md`, new section B5 heading "How wide an arrow's push is drawn — the rule, stated once" (uncommitted, +51/−18 total for the file), lines ~325–341:**

| Where the arrow came from | How wide the push is drawn |
|---|---|
| `documented` · `historical` · `market_implied` — somebody fetched something | `0.15` |
| `argued` · `user` — a stated mechanism, or a person's own judgement | `0.40` |
| `simulated` — a probe's output | `0.50` |
| `asserted` — a sentence with no mechanism in it | `0.60` |

The draw (`_version_strengths`, line 1507) is a stratified (Latin-hypercube) normal on the **log-odds scale**, centred on the stated strength, one stream per arrow:

```python
drawer = numpy.random.default_rng([seed, STRENGTHS_STREAM, _stream_key(arrow.id)])
strata = (drawer.permutation(versions) + drawer.random(versions)) / versions
steps = _standard_normal_quantile(strata)
drawn: Numbers = arrow.strength + steps * spreads[arrow.provenance]
```

And the push term in `_one_pass` became per-version × per-day:

```python
push = (strengths[arrow.id][:, None] * setup.shape_rows[arrow.id][None, :]).astype(DRAWING)
```

Explicit non-goals stated in the docstrings: **no `strength_lo` / `strength_hi`, ever** (cites Kent, decision record 0014); a drawn push never changes the *shape* of the map (retraction day and which arrows oppose a supposition are still read off the stated `strength`); and it is deliberately distinguished from `PROVENANCE_WEIGHT` at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py:139`:

> "Not to be confused with `PROVENANCE_WEIGHT` in `diff.py`… Two questions, two tables: one widens a band, the other ranks a row."

Provenance of the decision itself: `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/docs/adr/0014-a-supposition-ends-when-something-pushes-back.md:154` deferred it — *"A spread on link strengths derived from provenance… **Stack 04**, when the backing is real… **There are no `strength_lo` / `strength_hi` fields, ever**"*. ADR 0014 does **not** contain the numeric table; the table is new here.

### Tests

All in `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/tests/unit/domain/test_propagation.py` (+180/−9):

- **`test_a_documented_arrow_gives_a_narrower_band_than_an_asserted_one`** (line 1315) — one-arrow map, `documented < argued < asserted` band width; source claim's band stays `< 0.02`.
- **`test_link_spread_comes_only_from_provenance`** (line 1336) — for every word in `PROVENANCE_SPREAD`, mean of the draws is within `0.01` of the stated `1.2` and stdev within `0.02` of the table value; then two arrows differing in `mode`, `shape`, `lag`, `half_life`, `rationale`, `sources` but sharing a provenance must produce **bit-identical** draws (`numpy.array_equal`).
- **`test_adding_an_arrow_does_not_move_another_arrows_draws`** (line 1373) — adds a claim + arrow, asserts the new key set differs by exactly `{"middle->later"}` and every pre-existing arrow's draws are `array_equal`.
- **`test_band_is_not_sampling_noise`** (line 1143, rewritten) — now needs **two** freezes: `_frozen` (priors to points) **and** `_propagate_with_no_spread`. Asserts width `< 0.02` and `< 0.1 ×` the real band.
- **`test_freezing_the_priors_alone_leaves_the_arrows_talking`** (line 1166, new) — the complement: priors frozen, arrows still drawn ⇒ widest band `> 0.02`.
- **`test_range_matches_analytic_first_order_on_fixture`** (line 1188, rewritten) — the delta-method cross-check gained a per-arrow term (`_nudged`, line 1284, nudges one arrow's strength on the log-odds scale) and **the tolerance tightened from `.02` to `.01`**: `assert abs(...) < 0.01` on both `lo` and `hi`.

Helpers added: `_nudged` (1284), `_one_arrow_map` (1301), `_no_spread` (1181).

### Does it change the Hormuz demo numbers — yes

The spread moves numbers, and the worktree re-measured the spec tables (all uncommitted):

- `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`: H at Oct 5 `.080` → **`.086`**; C `.07` → **`.074`**; N1 `.37` → **`.38`**; the sustain survival "about eight in a hundred" → "about nine in a hundred"; B at days 1/2 now quoted as engine values `.039` / `.19`; B's band at day 45 `.35 (.20–.49)` → `.35 (.20–.50)`; the delta-method cross-check now reads *"the sampler reports `.2424–.5564` and the analytic answer is `.2394–.5562`"*; the base/branch table is annotated *"(Re-measured 2026-09-21… Every likelihood on this table is within a hundredth of what it was; **every band is wider**, N1's most of all…)"*, with N1 strike-branch = **`.38 (.17–.61)`** and R **byte-identical**.
- `spec/workbench/inspector.md`: B `.40 (.25–.55)` → **`.40 (.24–.56)`**; the range-share sentence `65% … 30 points to 12` → **`57% … 31 points to 16`**.
- `spec/multiverse/propagation.md` also now states the range-shares **do not sum to the band**: *"On B in the base world the seven shares total **72%**, and the missing quarter is the arrows."*

The **frontend is untouched by this worktree** — no `frontend/` file appears in the diff.

### Evidence for "on the strike branch two claims fall to `unchanged`"

Three independent artefacts.

## 2. The path product "moved into `domain/`" — it has **not** moved

There is **no** path-product code in `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/src/katalyst/domain/`. Every `domain/` hit for "product" is the English word ("this product"). The only implementation in the repo is unchanged from main.

### Where it actually lives

**`/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/src/katalyst/engine/verify.py`**

- **`_multiplied_out`, lines 139–167 (29 lines, 12 of them code).** File is 232 lines total.
- `git diff 48eb562 -- backend/src/katalyst/engine/verify.py` → **empty**. Same for `backend/tests/unit/engine/test_verify.py` and `backend/src/katalyst/api/generate.py`. This worktree does not touch any of them.

What it computes, exactly:

```python
    if beliefs is None:
        return None
    product = 1.0
    for claim_id in route[1:]:
        found = beliefs.get(claim_id)
        if found is None:
            return None
        product *= found.p
    return product
```

- The multiplied numbers are **`Belief.p`** — the propagated point likelihood — of each claim on the **best-backed route**, `route[1:]`, i.e. **the hypothesis is excluded** ("it is what the person is supposing happens, so it is not one of the steps that has to go right").
- **Which day each is read on:** each claim's own **resolve-by day** — that is the number a `World.beliefs[...]` carries. Hence the stated wart. `_multiplied_out`'s own docstring is explicit about the misplacement:

  > "The map's own arithmetic has no such number today — nothing in `domain/` multiplies a route out — so it is worked out here, over numbers the map produced. It moves the day it does."

- Supposed claims carry a stored `p = 1.0` (or `0.0`) precisely so this function has a factor; `spec/multiverse/propagation.md:281` says that value exists "for exactly one reader: the path product (INV-8)… **No other surface may read it.**"

### Route / API field

- `Verdict.product: float | None` — `verify.py:51`, described as *"The likelihoods along that route multiplied together. Nothing at all until the numbers have been worked through the map."*
- Populated at `verify.py:104`: `product=_multiplied_out(reached.path, beliefs)`.
- Carried on the wire by the **`verdict` SSE event** of the generation stream, emitted at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-evals/backend/src/katalyst/api/generate.py:526`: `yield verdict(finished.graph, finished.destination, beliefs=world.beliefs)`. Per `spec/generation/streaming.md:160`, the event appears **only** when the request named a `target`, and is ordered after `beliefs_propagated` because `product` is read off the propagated world.
